intended_object: A proof obligation: for each coordinate direction i, a particular set of (base point, line parameter) pairs is measurable. That set holds the pairs for which some admissible interval in the source window has a slice-measure average above t. Inferred from the docstring and from its use in `CoordinateSliceSourceLocalizedMaximalAverageExceedsMeasurable.badSetMeasurable`.
explanation: The body just applies `SourceLocalizedMaximalAverageExceedsMeasurable` (which is `MeasurableSet (sourceLocalizedMaximalAverageExceedsSet μparam t)`) to every coordinate i : Fin n. The docstring calls it a "measurability obligation". It is a named intermediate hypothesis in a step-by-step proof of the Aleksandrov theorem: a Fubini estimate for coordinate bad sets defined with a localized maximal function. The library uses it only to derive `CoordinateSliceMaximalBadSetMeasurable`, and it is itself derived from countable-interval cover hypotheses. It bundles proof-specific data (source windows, the `CoordinateSliceMeasureFamily` indexing, a threshold t). No standard mathematical notion in the literature corresponds to it. So it is an auxiliary proof device, not a mathematical object to compare against a textbook definition.
